item.title: Gert Small joins Flying Fijians coaching team ahead of November tests
item.description: Former South African Assistant coach Gert Small has been named as one of the coaches for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as the team prepares for the November test window. Small says he was part of the South African c oaching panel when Fiji played them in 2007 and came close to beating them.
item.content:encoded:
Former South African Assistant coach Gert Small has been named as one of the coaches for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as the team prepares for the November test window.

Small says he was part of the South African c oaching panel when Fiji played them in 2007 and came close to beating them.

He says he is really excited to be in Fiji and given a coaching role.

Small who was also part of the Ireland coaching team has a wealth of experience under his belt and he excited to coach players who are the best in the world .

He says adding structure and control to the Fijian brand of rugby will make Fiji a team to reckon with on the world stage.

Fiji will now look forward to Nations Championship next month, where they will face France on the 8th, Ireland on the 15th and Italy on the 22nd in their final match.

item.title: 14-year-old Khelan hopes to make family and Fiji proud at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: With the support of her family and faith in God, 14-year-old swimmer Grace-Elizabeth Khelan is hoping to make Fiji proud at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. The Jai Narayan College student, who is from Taveuni with maternal links to Tailevu, says her grandparents and mother have been her biggest motivation throughout her preparations.
item.content:encoded:
With the support of her family and faith in God, 14-year-old swimmer Grace-Elizabeth Khelan is hoping to make Fiji proud at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

The Jai Narayan College student, who is from Taveuni with maternal links to Tailevu, says her grandparents and mother have been her biggest motivation throughout her preparations.

Khelan says her mother has been waking her up for training and constantly encouraging her to put God first in everything she does.

She says preparations have been going well with the support of her swimming coach Esther Malani and her gym coach.

Khelan says her main goal is to reach the finals, achieve a personal best and hopefully bring home a medal for Fiji.

She is also encouraging other young athletes to never give up, keep working hard and always put God first.

Meanwhile, Fiji's Youth Olympic team and Deaf Rugby Sevens teams are scheduled to depart Fiji today.

The Youth Olympic Games will take place in Dakar, Senegal, from this Friday to November 13th, while the Deaf Rugby Sevens World Cup will be held from Saturday to next Tuesday.

Japan win sets platform for November tests - White
item.description: The victory over Japan's Brave Blossoms has set the platform for the team's November Test window. Speaking after the post-match interview, FIJI Water Flying Fijian Coach Jake White says it was good to be back coaching at the international level after 20 years.
item.content:encoded:
The victory over Japan's Brave Blossoms has set the platform for the team's November Test window.

Speaking after the post-match interview, FIJI Water Flying Fijian Coach Jake White says it was good to be back coaching at the international level after 20 years.

He said he felt like a kid in a candy shop, filled with excitement and joy.

White says the players knew what to do at the business end of the game and they understood the assigment set for them and he was proud of his players.

The team will now look forward to Nations Championship next month, where they will face France on the 8th, Ireland on the 15th and Italy on the 22nd in their final match.

item.title: Suva retain Futsal IDC title after impressive 5-2 win over Tailevu/Naitasiri
item.description: Suva delivered a strong performance to overcome their opponents and secure another championship title. The defending champions showed their attacking strength, scoring five goals to seal the victory and continue their winning run in the competition.
item.content:encoded:
Suva delivered a strong performance to overcome their opponents and secure another championship title.

The defending champions showed their attacking strength, scoring five goals to seal the victory and continue their winning run in the competition.

Despite Tailevu/Naitasiri finding the back of the net twice, Suva maintained their advantage to finish the match as champions.

Suva's Deepal Singh received Golden Boot Award.

item.title: White pleased with Flying Fijians game management in win over Japan
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians head coach Jake White says gaining control of the game and improving game management were key priorities in the team's 34–28 victory over Japan in Tokyo. Speaking during the post match interview, White says while Fiji are known for their attacking flair and ability to score spectacular tries, managing the closing stages of the match was particularly pleasing.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians head coach Jake White says gaining control of the game and improving game management were key priorities in the team's 34–28 victory over Japan in Tokyo.

Speaking during the post match interview, White says while Fiji are known for their attacking flair and ability to score spectacular tries, managing the closing stages of the match was particularly pleasing.

He says he was pleased with the team's performance in the final 10 to 15 minutes, where the team showed an improvement in an area that has been lacking for some time.

The team will now look forward to their northern tour next month, where they will face France on the 8th, Ireland on the 15th and Italy on the 22nd in their final match.

item.title: Fiji Bati prepare for tough test against Kangaroos tonight at 9.05pm
item.description: Vodafone Fiji Bati head coach Mick Potter says the team will focus on improving the areas where they fell short as they prepare for their blockbuster clash against the Kangaroos tonight. The Bati made a strong start to their 2026 Rugby League World Cup campaign, thumping the Cook Islands 40–12 in their opening match last Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Vodafone Fiji Bati head coach Mick Potter says the team will focus on improving the areas where they fell short as they prepare for their blockbuster clash against the Kangaroos tonight.

The Bati made a strong start to their 2026 Rugby League World Cup campaign, thumping the Cook Islands 40–12 in their opening match last Sunday.

Fiji scored seven tries to two to secure the win and currently top Pool A after the first round.

However, Potter says the team will be concentrating on addressing their shortcomings as they prepare to face Australia at 9.05pm tonight.

The match is expected to be a major test for the Bati as they look to build on their opening-round performance.

The Bati will face the Kangaroos at 9.05pm tonight.

In other matches today, New Zealand will take on the Cook Islands at 5.05pm, while England will face France at 6.35pm.
